name: 雅思
title: 雅思迷你模考
_說明: 題目全部原創。格式和 toeic.json 一樣；band_scale 是 [答對率下限, Band]，由高到低。audio 的句子開頭寫「男：」「女：」會換成 voices 裡的聲音。

parts.name: 聽力：日常對話
parts.intro: 聽一段電話對話，回答第 1–4 題。先看題目再播放，每段錄音最多可以播放 2 次。

audio: 女：Good morning, Riverside Cycle Hire. How can I help?
男：Hi, I'd like to rent a bike for a few days next week. I was thinking of a mountain bike, but I'll mostly be riding along the canal path into town.
女：Then a city bike would suit you better. It's lighter, and it comes with a basket and lights. The mountain bikes are really for the forest trails.
男：OK, a city bike it is. How much does it cost?
女：It's twelve pounds a day, or fifty pounds for a full week.
男：I only need it from Monday to Thursday, so that's four days, forty-eight pounds. Hmm. Actually, for two pounds more I could keep it for the weekend as well. I'll take the weekly rate.
女：Good choice. We also need a deposit. It used to be a hundred pounds in cash, but now we just keep a copy of your photo ID instead. A passport or a driving licence is fine.
男：Great. And could I pick it up on Sunday evening?
女：I'm afraid we close at four on Sundays, and the bike won't be ready until Monday. We open at eight thirty on weekdays, though most people come at around nine.
男：Eight thirty is perfect. I'll be there as soon as you open.

questions.q: Which type of bike does the man decide to rent?
questions.explain: 男生一開始說 I was thinking of a mountain bike，但店員建議 city bike 比較適合走運河步道，他回答 OK, a city bike it is，所以選 B。雅思聽力最常見的陷阱就是「先說一個、後來改掉」，要聽到最後的決定。

questions.q: How much will the man pay for the rental?
questions.explain: 一天 12 鎊、一週 50 鎊。他先算四天是 48 鎊（干擾項），接著說多 2 鎊就能用到週末，I'll take the weekly rate，所以付 50 鎊，選 C。

questions.q: What does the man need to leave as a deposit?
options: a copy of his photo ID
questions.explain: It used to be a hundred pounds in cash（以前是 100 鎊現金），but now…a copy of your photo ID instead。used to 表示「以前是、現在不是」，but now 後面才是答案，選 A。

questions.q: When will the man collect the bike?
questions.explain: 星期天四點就關門、車子星期一才準備好，所以不是 A。店員說平日 8:30 開門、多數人 9 點左右來（干擾項），男生說 Eight thirty is perfect，選 C。

parts.name: 聽力：日常獨白
parts.intro: 聽一段給博物館志工的說明，回答第 5–8 題。

audio: Welcome, everyone, and thank you for volunteering at the Harbour Museum. Before we start, a few practical things. You might expect our busiest day to be Saturday, but in fact it's Wednesday, when the school groups visit. So that's when we need most of you.

In the past, volunteers began in the gift shop or at the information desk. However, this season all new volunteers will start by helping in the children's gallery, where the hands-on activities take place. After a month, you can ask to move to another area.

Please wear your blue volunteer badge at all times. We'll give you one today. You don't need a uniform, just comfortable clothes and flat shoes. Lockers are available, but you must bring your own padlock.

Finally, lunch. The staff canteen is closed for repairs until March, so you won't be able to eat there. Instead, you'll get a voucher for the café on the ground floor, which gives you a free hot drink and half-price food.

questions.q: Which is the museum's busiest day?
questions.explain: You might expect…Saturday, but in fact it's Wednesday。「你可能以為是星期六，但其實是星期三」，but in fact 後面才是答案，選 C。

questions.q: Where will new volunteers work first this season?
questions.explain: In the past（以前）志工從禮品店或服務台開始；However, this season（但是這一季）全部新志工先到 children's gallery 幫忙，選 B。In the past 和 However 是時間對比的訊號。

questions.q: What must volunteers bring themselves?
questions.explain: 徽章今天會發（We'll give you one today）、不需要制服（You don't need a uniform），只有置物櫃的鎖要自己帶：you must bring your own padlock，選 A。

questions.q: What will volunteers receive at lunchtime?
options: a free meal in the staff canteen
questions.explain: 員工餐廳整修到三月不能用，所以 A 錯。改發一樓咖啡廳的券：a free hot drink and half-price food，免費的只有熱飲，餐點是半價，選 B。

parts.name: 閱讀：是非無判斷
parts.intro: 閱讀文章，判斷第 9–14 題的敘述：和文章相符選 TRUE，和文章相反選 FALSE，文章沒有提到選 NOT GIVEN。

groups.passage:
The Return of the Night Train

For much of the twentieth century, sleeper trains linked almost every major European city. A traveller could board in Paris after dinner and wake up in Vienna. By the early 2000s, however, most of these services had disappeared. Cheap flights were the main cause: once budget airlines began selling tickets for less than the price of a restaurant meal, few passengers were willing to spend twelve hours on a train.

Night trains were also expensive to run. A sleeping car carries far fewer passengers than an ordinary carriage, yet it needs more staff, and it earns money only once a day, whereas a daytime train can make several journeys. Several national railway companies concluded that the services could never make a profit, and sold or scrapped their sleeping cars.

In the last decade the picture has changed. Concern about the carbon emissions of flying has led some travellers to look for alternatives. One national railway, which bought sleeping cars that other operators no longer wanted, now runs more night services than any other company in Europe. Its managers say the trains attract not only tourists but also business travellers. Problems remain, though: new sleeping cars take years to build, and on popular routes beds sell out months in advance.

questions.q: Low-cost airlines were the most important reason why night trains declined.
questions.explain: 第一段：Cheap flights were the main cause。main cause 就是 the most important reason 的換句話說，budget airlines＝low-cost airlines，選 TRUE。

questions.q: A sleeping car can carry about the same number of passengers as a normal carriage.
questions.explain: 第二段：A sleeping car carries far fewer passengers than an ordinary carriage（載的人少很多），和題目說的「差不多一樣多」相反，選 FALSE。

questions.q: Night trains use more electricity than daytime trains.
questions.explain: 文章說夜車貴在載客少、人手多、一天只賺一趟，完全沒有比較用電量，選 NOT GIVEN。不要因為「聽起來合理」就選 TRUE，文章沒寫的就是 NOT GIVEN。

questions.q: Some railway companies got rid of their sleeping cars.
questions.explain: 第二段最後：Several national railway companies…sold or scrapped their sleeping cars（賣掉或報廢）。got rid of 就是這個意思，選 TRUE。

questions.q: The new night services are used only by tourists.
questions.explain: 第三段：attract not only tourists but also business travellers（不只觀光客，還有商務旅客）。題目的 only 和文章相反，選 FALSE。題目出現 only、all、always 這類絕對的字要特別小心。

questions.q: Tickets for night trains are cheaper than flights on most routes.
questions.explain: 文章只說以前便宜機票搶走乘客，沒有比較現在夜車和機票哪個便宜，選 NOT GIVEN。

parts.name: 閱讀：選擇與句子填空
parts.intro: 閱讀文章，回答第 15–20 題。第 15–17 題選出正確答案；第 18–20 題選出最適合填入空格的字詞。

groups.passage:
Why We Forget Names

Most people have had the experience of being introduced to someone and forgetting the person's name within seconds. Psychologists suggest that this is not a sign of a poor memory. The real problem is attention: at the moment of introduction we are usually busy thinking about what we are going to say next, so the name is never properly stored in the first place.

Names are also unusually hard to remember because they are arbitrary. If you learn that a woman is a baker, the word brings to mind bread, ovens and early mornings, and these connections help to fix the fact in memory. If you learn that her surname is Baker, however, the word tells you nothing about her. In one well-known experiment, people who were shown a face together with the word 'baker' remembered it far better when they were told it was the person's job than when they were told it was the person's name.

The solution, researchers say, is to create the connections that names lack. Repeating the name aloud during the conversation helps a little. A more effective method is to link the name to an image, the stranger and more vivid the better. Writing names down afterwards is useful for later reference, but it does little to strengthen the memory itself.

questions.q: According to the first paragraph, people forget names mainly because
options: they meet too many new people.
they are not paying attention when they hear the name.
questions.explain: 第一段：this is not a sign of a poor memory（不是記憶力差，A 錯），The real problem is attention（真正的問題是注意力），因為當下忙著想自己接下來要說什麼，選 C。

questions.q: The 'baker' experiment showed that people remember a word better when
options: it is connected with other things they know.
it is shown together with a face.
questions.explain: 同一個字 baker，當成「職業」比當成「姓氏」記得牢，因為職業會聯想到麵包、烤箱（these connections help to fix the fact in memory）。所以關鍵是「有沒有連結」，選 A。C 是陷阱：兩組人都有看到臉，不是差別所在。

questions.q: Which method does the writer say is the most effective?
options: asking the person to repeat it
linking the name to an unusual image
questions.explain: 第三段：唸出名字 helps a little（只有一點幫助）；A more effective method is to link the name to an image, the stranger…the better（更有效的是連結到圖像，越怪越好），選 D。寫下來 does little to strengthen the memory，B 錯；C 文章沒提。

questions.q: Names are difficult to remember because they are ______, which means they tell us nothing about the person.
questions.explain: 第二段第一句：Names are also unusually hard to remember because they are arbitrary（任意的、沒有道理可循的）。填空題的答案通常就是原文的字，回到文章找同一句，選 B。

questions.q: When we learn a person's ______, the word reminds us of related things.
questions.explain: 第二段：知道她是 baker（麵包師）會想到麵包、烤箱、清晨；知道她「姓」Baker 卻什麼也想不到。會帶來聯想的是職業，選 C。A 剛好相反，是這題的陷阱。

questions.q: Writing names down is helpful for ______ but does not improve memory much.
questions.explain: 最後一句：useful for later reference（方便之後查看），但 does little to strengthen the memory itself。later reference 換句話說就是 checking later，選 D。

advice.L1: 日常對話最常考「先說一個答案、後來改掉」：聽到 but、actually、instead、used to 就要注意，答案通常在轉折後面。建議先花 30 秒看題目、圈出關鍵字（數字、時間、物品），再邊聽邊刪去被否定的選項。
advice.L2: 獨白題的訊號字是時間對比（in the past／this season）和 but in fact、however。三個選項通常都會被唸到，但只有一個符合題目問的。建議練習聽完一段就用自己的話說出重點，再對照逐字稿找漏聽的地方。
advice.R1: TRUE／FALSE／NOT GIVEN 要分清楚：文章有寫而且相反才是 FALSE，文章根本沒比較、沒提到就是 NOT GIVEN。題目裡的 only、all、most 這類字常是關鍵。建議每題都回文章畫出對應的句子，找不到句子就選 NOT GIVEN。
advice.R2: 選擇題和填空題的答案幾乎都是文章句子的「換句話說」（later reference＝checking later）。先看題目的關鍵字、回文章定位到那一句，再比對選項。建議平常整理同義替換的字，也可以搭配單字庫加強學術字彙。
